what_changed.text: Status jumps from Emerging Disorder — Stable to Crisis Acceleration — Transition — and not from the signal you'd expect. Tier 1 is quiet (1/10). The escalation is Override Rule #5: private-credit fund gates appearing in the same month the Fed is still expanding its balance sheet. The framework was built to fire on exactly this configuration.

Four flagship private-credit funds gated redemptions in H1 2026 — Blue Owl, BlackRock's HPS Lending Fund, Morgan Stanley's North Haven, and Apollo's Debt Solutions vehicle. Blackstone avoided a gate only by injecting its own capital against $3.8B of requests. Private Credit Stress steps from 0 to 2.

Brent fell to $78 on the US–Iran de-escalation and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz — yet the Oil/SPR Capacity Ratio rose to 229 and the score climbed back to 2. The March emergency drained 172M barrels (the US share of a coordinated 400M release), leaving the reserve near 340M (~48% of capacity). Lower price, far less buffer.

Gold cooled to $4,153, +23% YoY with 8-week momentum at −9.5%, and the Gold/Treasury Divergence stays at baseline as yields firmed to ~4.5%. Tiers move to T1=1/10, T2=8/20, T3=3/12. The marquee Tier 1 signals are dormant — this transition is being driven by the plumbing, not the monetary-momentum complex.

contrarian: Wall Street sees gold off its highs, oil back below $80, and the dollar firm, and calls the all-clear. The Canary reads the opposite. The stress didn't dissipate — it migrated. It left the monetary-momentum signals (gold, the divergence) and reappeared in the credit plumbing: four private-credit funds slammed the redemption window shut in a single half-year. A crisis that changes venue is not a crisis that ended.

A gate is a confession. When a fund suspends redemptions, it is telling you the marks on its book cannot survive contact with real exit demand. Blue Owl, BlackRock, Morgan Stanley, and Apollo all did exactly that while the Fed quietly expanded its balance sheet at $40B/month. That specific pairing — illiquid-credit stress alongside monetary accommodation — is Override Rule #5, and it is the configuration the framework was designed to catch early. It is live now.

Oil at $78 looks like relief. It isn't. The Strategic Petroleum Reserve sits near 340M barrels — under half of capacity — after March's 172M-barrel emergency draw. The 2022 circuit breaker required 180M barrels at $120 oil; there is no longer that much dry powder in the reserve, and no political will to refill it. The price came down while the vulnerability went up. The framework scores the buffer, not the headline.

divergence.description: The single most predictive indicator in The Canary. When gold surges and yields don't follow, the bond market is being artificially suppressed — either through direct purchases or implicit policy. This divergence preceded every major regime transition in the last 50 years.
divergence.current_reading: Current reading: Gold is +23% YoY while the 10Y has firmed to ~4.5% — the gap that defined this cycle has closed from the gold side. Gold peaked near $5,300 in January and has since cooled to $4,153, while yields drifted up rather than down. The Gold/Treasury Divergence — the framework's most predictive indicator — has gone quiet, and it is not what is driving this escalation. That is the point worth sitting with: the regime moved to Transition with the marquee signal dormant. The stress is now in credit, not in the bond–gold spread. When a transition fires without the divergence, the system is telling you the next leg runs through the plumbing.

consensus.wall_street: Idiosyncratic — a few funds managing liquidity prudently.
consensus.atlas: Four flagship funds gating in one half-year is not idiosyncratic. With the Fed expanding simultaneously, it trips Override Rule #5 → immediate Transition.

consensus.wall_street: The run is over; the safe-haven bid has faded.
consensus.atlas: Gold +23% YoY, consolidating after a ~$5,300 peak. Cooling momentum is not reversal — and the escalation isn't coming from gold anyway.

consensus.wall_street: Energy risk resolved — Hormuz reopened, supply normalizing.
consensus.atlas: SPR near 48% after the 172M-bbl March draw. Lower price, depleted buffer — the ratio rose to 229. The circuit breaker is spent.
Balance sheet still expanding at $40B/mo. That expansion is half of the Override #5 trigger now firing.

consensus.wall_street: Baa spreads benign — no systemic stress.
consensus.atlas: Spreads lag gates. Redemption suspensions are the leading signal; spreads are the confirmation that hasn't arrived yet.
TC/RCs still negative — smelters paying miners. The structural concentrate shortage is unmoved by the macro tape.

positioning.intro: The status escalates to Crisis Acceleration — Transition. The trigger is not gold — it's Override Rule #5: private-credit gates plus an expanding Fed, firing in the same month. This is the phase the framework was built to flag early, when the largest moves in hard assets historically occur. The short-term Treasury buffer now begins to wind down — Transition is the point where the framework starts treating Treasuries themselves as part of the problem, not the parking lot.

posture.label: Gold — overweight
posture.reason: Tier 1 is quiet, but the structural case is intact: a Fed still expanding, central banks buying 244t in Q1 (≈976t annualized), and a credit system that just started gating. Gold's pullback to $4,153 is consolidation inside a monetary regime change, not its end. Add on weakness.

posture.label: Bitcoin — overweight
posture.reason: High-beta gold. In a credit-led transition, BTC is the cleanest expression of the monetary-accommodation response that follows forced liquidity. Size for volatility — it will draw down with risk assets before it leads.

posture.label: Short-term Treasuries — reduce
posture.reason: Transition is the wind-down point. The T-bill buffer that made sense at Elevated now starts coming off as the framework shifts to treating Treasuries as the problem rather than the parking lot. Keep only what funds near-term liquidity.

posture.label: Critical materials — overweight
posture.reason: Copper TC/RCs still negative, silver in a sixth straight deficit year. The Material Ledger doesn't care about the macro tape — physical tightness is unmoved by gold's pullback or oil's drop.

posture.label: Equities — underweight
posture.reason: S&P/Gold at 1.80 — nominal highs masking a multi-year loss of purchasing power in gold terms. A credit-led transition is precisely when equity multiples are most exposed.

posture.label: Long Treasuries — underweight
posture.reason: Yields firmed to ~4.5% against a Fed still buying and a credit system gating. Long duration carries asymmetric downside when forced liquidity meets a depleted fiscal buffer.

escalation: A fifth or sixth private-credit gate, or a gate that drags in a bank counterparty → pushes Private Credit Stress toward systemic and Tier 2 higher.
Fed shifts to long-duration purchases (Override #4) → immediate confirmation. Currently bills-only.
Treasury auction B/C drops below 2.0 → demand crisis. Currently firm (10Y 2.45, 30Y 2.43) — watch the next refunding.
Gold 8-week momentum recovers above +10% → Tier 1 re-engages on top of the credit signal. Currently −9.5%.
deescalation: Gated funds reopen redemptions in orderly fashion → Override #5 clears. None have reopened yet.
Fed resumes QT at full pace → removes half the Override #5 trigger. Balance sheet still growing at $40B/mo.
SPR refill begins at scale → restores the oil circuit breaker. No refill underway; reserve near 48% of capacity.
Tier 2 falls back below 6 with no active overrides → returns to Stable. Currently 8/20 with Override #5 live.

track_record.intro: Applied retroactively across nine historical periods, The Canary identified every major regime transition 3–6 months early with near-zero false positives.

adversarial.label: Gold rally (+25%)
adversarial.result: No signal ✔ — cyclical bounce with no yield divergence or Fed expansion. Gold reversed within a year.

adversarial.label: Gold bear market (−45%)
adversarial.result: No false signal ✔ — real tightening with rising yields. The system correctly read this as non-monetary.

adversarial.label: Fed tightening cycle
adversarial.result: No false signal ✔ — QT was running and balance sheet shrinking. No divergence to trigger on.

adversarial.label: LTCM / Russia crisis
adversarial.result: Correctly filtered ✔ — financial stress but no monetary regime implications. Fed cut rates and markets stabilized.

adversarial.label: SVB banking stress
adversarial.result: Brief signal, self-corrected ✔ — initial spike in Fed lending resolved within weeks. No sustained monetary shift.

adversarial.label: 30-year balance sheet expansion
adversarial.result: Right on direction, open on timing — BOJ's experiment is still running. The framework flags the trajectory correctly but can't call the endpoint.
